FERTILIZERS STOCKS : CABINET APPROVES CONTINUATION OF PM-KISAN SCHEME 🌾

• 🌾 Cabinet approves continuation of PM-KISAN for FY27–FY31 with a total outlay of ₹3.16 lakh crore

• 💰 Eligible landholding farmer families will continue to receive ₹6,000 per year in three DBT instalments of ₹2,000 each

• 👨‍🌾 Scheme aligned with crop cycles to support farmers during Kharif sowing, harvest and Rabi season

• 📈 Government expects to provide ₹4.47 lakh crore in direct income support across 23 instalments

• 🌱 Aims to improve farmers' liquidity, reduce dependence on informal credit and support purchase of seeds, fertilizers and other farm inputs

• 🌾 Around 85% of beneficiaries are small and marginal farmers, supporting inclusive rural growth

🟢 Likely Beneficiaries: Coromandel International, Paradeep Phosphates, Chambal Fertilisers, RCF, NFL, FACT, PI Industries, UPL, Dhanuka Agritech, Kaveri Seed, Godrej Agrovet and other agri-input companies.

RENEWABLES STOCKS ; CABINET APPROVES PM SURYA SAROVAR YOJANA ☀️🌊

• ⚡ Cabinet approves Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY) with a total outlay of ₹5,070 crore

• 🌞 Targets 5,000 MW of Floating Solar PV (FSPV) capacity over 5 years, up from around 700 MW currently

• 💰 Provides ₹1 crore/MW support under the scheme

• 🔋 All projects to include minimum 2-hour Energy Storage Systems (ESS) totalling 10,000 MWh

• 💧 Floating solar projects to utilize reservoirs, canals and industrial ponds, reducing land requirement and water evaporation while improving generation efficiency

• 🏭 Expected to boost domestic manufacturing of floating solar systems, anchoring, mooring and energy storage components, while creating 16,000–17,000 jobs and reducing 10 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually

🟢 Likely Beneficiaries: NTPC, NHPC, SJVN, KPI Green Energy, Waaree Energies, Premier Energies, Tata Power Renewable Energy, Adani Green Energy, Suzlon, Inox Wind, battery storage and floating solar ecosystem companies.

OIL EXPLORATION STOCKS ; CABINET APPROVES ₹84,084 CR ‘SAMUDRA MANTHAN’ SCHEME 🌊🛢️

• 🇮🇳 Cabinet approves Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme with a total outlay of ₹84,084 crore

• 🎯 Aims to enhance India's domestic oil & gas reserves and production while strengthening energy security

• 🌊 ₹28,500+ crore allocated for offshore 2D/3D seismic data acquisition, processing & interpretation

• 🛢️ ₹43,200 crore earmarked to support drilling of 60 deepwater & ultra-deepwater exploration wells by public and private E&P companies

• ⚙️ ₹10,000 crore for common offshore infrastructure to commercialise stranded discoveries

• 🏭 ₹2,000 crore to establish Oil & Gas Manufacturing & Services Zones under the Make in India initiative

🟢 Likely Beneficiaries: ONGC, Oil India, Hindustan Oil Exploration Company (HOEC), Oil & Natural Gas service providers, offshore EPC and equipment manufacturers.

Sterlite Tech: Nuvama Report and my thoughts

Nuvama has come up with an updated report on Sterlite Tech with a price target of 770.

Their earlier price target was 440, which they increased to 770 after Q11FY27 results..
That's an upgrade of 75%
Just imagine the amount of earnings surprise.

Before Q1Fy27 results, many brokerages were expecting Sterlite to generate a PAT of 400-500 crores in FY27
Now, the same brokerages are estimating FY27 PAT to be 900-100 Crores, almost an increase of 100%

Nuvama report estimates Fy27 PAT of 906 Cr.
However, this is still conservative and below the management guidance  - Nuvama has considered EBITDA margins of 20.3% whereas Company has guided for 23%

Also, Sterlite recently did a QIP of 1500 Cr. While this will lead to a dilution of 5%, the entire debt is gone on one shot and it has become a net cash company !!

Personally, I think Sterlite would cross 1000 Cr PAT for FY 27 easily and might hit 1100 Cr.

Now, the interesting part - valuations
Before Q1FY27 results, Sterlite was trading at a trailing PE of 500+. Many people looked at screener PE, and shouted bubble !!
Now, PE has already dropped to 121
On FY27 basis - Sterlite is trading at a PE of 30-32
Half of the stocks in the Indian market are trading at higher valuations !!

Always consider forward earnings and valuations.
Particularly for turnaround cases like Sterlite, it is futile to look at trailing PE !!

Company Overview:
Advit Jewels Limited is a Jaipur-based luxury jewellery company specializing in Kundan, Polki, Diamond, and Studded Jewellery. Backed by a family legacy dating back to 1921, the Company follows an integrated business model encompassing in-house design, manufacturing, stone setting, polishing, and quality control, serving customers across India through its design-led and quality-focused approach.

Business & Operational Highlights:

Customer & Market Presence
* Active customer base increased from 96 to 274, with presence across 21 states.
* Continued strengthening its position in the premium bridal jewellery segment through a diversified customer base.

Product Portfolio & Manufacturing
* Specializes in Kundan, Meena, Polki, Jadau handcrafted jewellery.
* Strong design capabilities and a stable artisan ecosystem backed by over 100 years of jewellery craftsmanship.

Growth & Strategic Initiatives:

Retail Expansion
* Plans to establish 30 franchise stores over the next three years.
* Targeting the opening of at least three stores during FY27.
* A 30,000 sq. ft. flagship store in Jaipur, is expected to commence operations by this year.

Product & Market Expansion
* Expanding into men's luxury jewellery, including cufflinks, brooches and belt buckles.
* Launching a dedicated Gen-Z jewellery collection featuring lightweight, everyday luxury designs.
* Exploring export opportunities in the UK and Middle East, while strengthening domestic retail operations.

Management Commentary & Outlook:
* Remains confident of long-term growth driven by retail expansion, product diversification and increasing brand recognition.
* Focus will remain on premium craftsmanship, disciplined execution, customer experience and sustainable long-term value creation for shareholders.

Key Takeaways:
* Delivered strong double-digit growth in revenue, EBITDA and profitability during FY26.
* Successfully completed listing on the NSE and BSE, marking a significant milestone in the Company's growth journey.
* Retail expansion through franchise stores and the Jaipur flagship showroom is expected to strengthen direct consumer engagement.

Company Update | UniHealth Hospitals Receives Prestigious Healthcare Excellence Award

UniHealth Hospitals has been honoured with the Emerging Multispeciality Hospital of the Year award at the NavaBharat Healthcare Summit & Awards 2026, held at Hotel Taj President, Mumbai, on July 29, 2026.

The award was received on behalf of the Company by its Promoter & Managing Director, Dr. Akshay Parmar, recognising UniHealth Hospitals' commitment to clinical excellence, patient-centric care, and quality healthcare delivery.

The event was graced by Shri Prakash Abitkar, Hon'ble Health Minister, Government of Maharashtra, as the Chief Guest, and Ms. Shaina NC, Shiv Sena Leader, as the Special Guest.

So why did PBT jump +138% and PAT +156% when EBITDA fell?

The gap sits almost entirely below EBITDA and is non-operating. 

The clue is the "share of profit of Joint Ventures" line and the reconciliation: PBT of ₹868.98 Cr is far above what ₹463 Cr of EBITDA minus ₹107 Cr depreciation minus ₹24 Cr finance cost (≈₹332 Cr operating PBT) would produce. 

The ~₹537 Cr difference comes from other income of ₹528.29 Cr — which exploded from just ₹1.68 Cr a year ago. 

That single line is the entire story of the profit surge. 

A ₹528 Cr other-income figure on this base is not routine treasury income; 

it's almost certainly a one-off/exceptional item (a fair-value gain, a stake revaluation, a divestment/JV-related gain, or similar). Because your EBITDA definition strips other income, EBITDA correctly shows the flat operating reality while PBT/PAT capture the windfall.

This is the trickiest quarter of the set, and the headline EPS (+154%) and PBT (+138%) badly overstate the operating quarter — read it carefully. Revenue grew a strong +21% YoY, consistent with continued EMS/mobile ramp, and operationally that's the real story. But operating EBITDA actually fell ~4% YoY, and the EBITDA margin compressed to 2.98% from 3.76% — a ~78 bps decline. 

For a thin-margin assembler this is the line that matters: the revenue mix is shifting even more toward ultra-low-margin, high-value mobile assembly (BOM pass-through), which dilutes the blended margin even as it inflates the topline. So the operating engine ran roughly flat-to-slightly-down YoY on absolute EBITDA despite 21% more revenue — the opposite of what the EPS suggests.

• Management reaffirmed its operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000 crores to INR7,700 crores for FY27, citing strong demand tailwinds, a record order book, and on-schedule expansion projects.

• The company projects its retail business to achieve INR9,000 crores to INR10,000 crores in revenue for the full year FY27.

• The announced CapEx program totals approximately INR31,500 crores, with INR9,450 crores deployed by June 30, and is phased with 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28, and 30% in FY29.

text:
Jefferies on HUL

Buy, TP Rs 2850

While HUL's 1Q was a slight miss, 7% share price drop is baffling given extent of miss.

There were a few weak spots (Home Care margins; growth in Personal Care & Foods), but offsetting factors meant the overall miss in EBITDA was small.

Also note consistent improvement in growth & profitability over past few qtrs.

Mgmt. commentary was reasonable, with expectations of stable demand & margin remaining in the guided range.

Macquarie on Chola Invest

U-P, TP Rs 1495

Delivered a strong 1Q FY27, with PAT rising 46% YoY to Rs16.5bn, broadly in line with estimates.

Better cost-to-income of 36% (vs 40% MQe) offset softer-than-expected 8.2% NIM (vs 8.5% MQe).

Credit cost was broadly in line, while AUM grew 22% YoY, led by LAP, SBPL, and SME.

RoA expanded 50bps YoY to 2.8%.

Despite decent performance, valuation remains stretched at a 3.4x FY28E P/BV, assuming 2.7% ROA

CLSA on Chola Invest

O-P, TP Rs 1970

3% PAT beat vs estimates in 1QFY27, driven by a 5% PPOP beat, partly offset by higher-than-expected credit costs.

Overall, it was a good quarter.

Disbursement and AUM growth both were in the low-20s while NIM was largely stable on a sequential basis.

Stronger-than-expected fees and lower-than-expected opex helped drive the beat on PPOP.

Asset quality improved with the calculated net slippage ratio declining 40bps YoY to 2.5% driven by an improvement in vehicle finance and CSEL; there is room for further reduction as it is still above 1QFY25 levels.

Management sounded confident on the analyst call.

HSBC on Chola Invest

Buy, TP Rs 2140

1Q underscored by healthy AUM growth, margin trends, and strong asset quality

Raise EPS by 0.9/3.1/7.9% for FY27/28/29e respectively as raise AUM growth, NIM & lower credit costs

CIFC looks attractive relative to peers & trades at 3.3x FY28e BVPS / 17.5x EPS, a discount of 19% in PB / 17% in PE to BAF

JPM on Varun Beverages

Neutral, TP Rs 530

Management tried to address key investor concerns, though a few pressure points remain visible.

Even as domestic volume growth is trending 20%+ in most months, weather-related disruptions can still weigh on reported growth, as witnessed in Q2 (April flat).

Management sounded confident of sustaining healthy double-digit growth, though delivery is increasingly reliant on sharper Rs20 propositions and scale-up of adjacencies

Competitive intensity remains elevated, particularly at lower price points (aiding category expansion), and VBL is prioritizing profitable growth over aggressively chasing low-margin Rs10 volumes.

International territories continue to fare well, led by broad-based Africa momentum, though Twizza integration/scale-up and Kenya expansion (post acquisition) will be key watch points.

VBL trades at 39x/34x CY27/28E P/E
Although see limited downside at current levels, domestic volume growth delivery (1HCY26 2 yr CAGR +~8%) will be a key share price catalyst.
Mirae Asset Sharekhan Morning Tiger ( Pre - Market Insight ) - 29th July 2026.pdf

CITI on Varun Beverages

Buy, TP cut to Rs 580 from Rs 640

India volumes grew 14% (off a -7% base) primarily impacted by weather-led disruption in April.

Key investor debate at VBL remains whether growth trajectory has structurally moderated amid increased competitive intensity in India; note that despite competitive pressures, India volumes delivered an 8% CAGR over past two years in 1HCY26.

Going ahead, while mgmt. commentary remains constructive, calling out sustained 20%+ volume growth trends extending into July, note that 2H accounts for only 35% of annual volumes. 

Believe category remains attractive (penetration-led growth opportunity) over long-term & competitive intensity could be gradually easing with Campa reducing volumes in its Rs10 SKU – we would look for an acceleration in 2-year CAGR trajectory.

CITI on SAIL 

Sell, TP Rs 160 

1Q EBITDA rose 72% yoy largely on higher realizations (+13%); volumes fell 9%, costs rose 4%. 

Adj EBITDA/t: Rs10,715 vs. Rs8,280 in 4Q; Rs5,695 last year. 

QoQ EBITDA/t move – higher realizations (Rs5,870/t), offset by higher costs (~Rs3,430). 

Call highlights: 

1) 1Q volumes fell ~9% yoy -planned shutdowns, SAIL is maintaining FY27 volume target at ~13%. 

2) July flats prices at Rs56,900 vs. Rs57,200 in 1Q; longs at Rs54,200 vs. Rs57,100. 

3) Coking coal higher qoq in 1Q, SAIL expects a reduction in Aug/Sep. 

4) 1Q wage costs rose on VRS, wage revision due in Jan27. 

5) SAIL is targeting cost savings by FY29. 6) Net debt Rs217bn, FY27/28 capex Rs150bn/Rs200bn

 Sell: (1) Likely downside to EBITDA/t – domestic weakness + limited China upside, 

(2) Limited growth potential, next leg of capacities after 3 years, 

(3) Estimate net D/EBITDA at 2.5x+ by FY28.

CLSA on Supreme Ind

Hold, TP Rs 4000

Q1 in-line , as weak sales volumes (-14% YoY) were partly offset by higher margins (on a better mix).

Management maintained its FY27 guidance of 12%-13% volume growth & a 14%-14.5% Ebitda margin

This looks demanding, despite recovering PVC prices, given ask rate for the rest of year is 20%+ on a high base.

🚨 Capri Global starts FY27 with a strong quarter.

Some numbers that stood out:

📌 Net Profit doubled YoY to ₹353 Cr
📌 AUM crossed ~₹40,000 Cr with 62% growth
📌 ROAE improved to 19.1%

Branch network now at 1,433, loan book remains 100% secured and collateralised.

Profit growth outpacing AUM growth points to improving unit economics and scale.

__Shared for informational purposes only. Not investment advice.__

CITI on Supreme Ind

Sell, TP Rs 3150

1Q EBITDA was up 25% yoy despite 14% lower volumes (channel destocking) on higher EBITDA margins (14.6% vs 12.2% in 1QFY26).

EBITDA margin improvement was likely driven by a combination of lower cost PVC inventory, better product mix, and inventory loss recorded in 1QFY26.

Plastic piping segment volumes were down ~15% yoy, EBIT/kg was Rs16.3/kg vs 19.9/kg in 4Q and Rs10.6/kg in 1QFY26.

Looking ahead, mgmt. has reiterated their guidance for 15-17% volume growth in the plastic piping segment (12-13% overall).

This implies a 26% yoy volume growth in piping segment for balance 9MFY27.

Considering modest growth indicated by mgmt. for May/Jun (in a relatively stable PVC price environment), think there could be downside risk to the FY27 volume guidance.

GS on L&T

Buy, TP Rs 4370

L&T's P&M (core) order inflow was 17% yoy in 1QFY27 (vs. GSe of -6%), and 1Q core EBITDA margins came in at 6.9% (vs. GSe of 7.1%) a 20bps decline yoy, driven by lower execution in core segments.

Key highlights from quarter:

1) Prospect base being resilient at Rs15tn despite strong order inflow in Q1 and well spread across domestic as well as international with private sector representing 45% in the mix.

2) Project execution continued to be impacted amid West Asia conflict, reflected in weaker execution;

3) FY27 guidance maintained at +10-12% on order inflows and similar growth in revenue with core margins flat (7.8% excluding realty biz. and 8.2% including realty).

Mgt highlighted that award and tendering in ME continues.

Jefferies on L&T

Buy, TP Rs 5000

Q1 EBITDA was 8% lower than expectations as E&C execution was weak.

14% YoY rise in order flow is tracking L&T’s annual 10-12% YoY growth guidance.

Management maintained its annual 10-12% YoY revenue guidance, implying that 2H will be better, but likely conditional on war settling down

Believe L&T stock should see a leg up to Rs4278 (when conflict started) if global tensions ease, with earnings visibility adding to upside thereon.

India Built a Phone Export Industry. Now It Needs Customers It Doesn't Have.

India's handset export scheme is aimed at a global market where roughly 61% of units sit outside Apple and Samsung and are served by Chinese brands using Chinese assemblers. The binding constraint is therefore anchor customer access, not incentive quantum or installed capacity, which is why the same policy tool that worked domestically may not repeat offshore. 

This is falsified if a non Apple Indian assembler announces a multi year export contract with a top ten global brand.
